Keep the Expedition in Northern Italy

The northern rising presents a choice between domestic retreat and an Italian campaign. Keep the expedition in the field and declare war on Austria for the liberation of Lombardy and Venetia. Victory would restore those lands to their Italian states, leaving their later political settlement open. The crown must secure the south and arrange military access before its army can march north.

The Northern Expedition Vindicated

Austria has accepted the liberation terms. The Lombard and Venetian lands covered by the treaty pass to their own states. The expedition has won Naples a place in the national struggle, but no northern court has thereby surrendered its independence.

The Expedition Returns without a Settlement

The northern campaign has ended without the liberation terms being accepted. The army returns to a kingdom still divided over the expedition. Ministers must explain why its sacrifices did not secure a northern settlement.

The Italian Brothers' War

The Italian Initiative Passes to Naples

The treaty has established the southern initiative and binds the defeated Savoyard kingdom to incorporation. The annexation articles will be implemented after the Papal and northern diplomatic offices confirm the peace. The other Italian courts retain their own accession choices.
The ministry must answer for the defeat.
The Southern Challenge Has Failed

The war has ended without southern recognition. If Piedmont enforced its own leadership demand, the southern Italian sphere has been broken in turn. The court must confront the failure of its campaign, and the planned accession initiative cannot proceed on the strength of this war.
Demand a Settlement in the Papal Provinces

Demand Benevento, Pontecorvo, Perugia and Ancona where they remain papal, with the remaining Papal State placed under southern protection. The Pope may accept or refuse, opening a war claim. France may oppose the proposal. A later Roman settlement will require victory over Piedmont and guarantees for the Holy See.
Offer a Federal Settlement to Rome

Offer regional guarantees for Benevento, Pontecorvo, Perugia and Ancona, with the remaining Papal State becoming a protected member under the southern crown. Refusal can lead to a war claim. The Pope retains his government, while any later integration requires victory over Piedmont and guarantees for the Holy See.
Reject the territorial demand.
Accept the protectorate and cede the agreed provinces.
The Southern Proposal for the Papal Provinces

Naples demands Benevento, Pontecorvo, Perugia and Ancona wherever they remain under papal rule. The remaining Papal State would retain its Pope and government as a dependent principality under southern protection. Federal envoys offer regional guarantees, while the other programmes propose central administration for the ceded provinces. Refusal may lead to war and French intervention.
Maintain the claim.
Withdraw the demand.
The Pope Rejects the Demand

The Pope has rejected the provincial articles and southern protection. His answer is now before our ministers. We can withdraw the demand or maintain the claim. A war to enforce it still requires our active Italian mandate, independence and control of Naples. Victory must secure the Papal settlement as a peace term: the agreed provinces would pass to our government and the remaining Papal State would become a protected principality. France retains its freedom to intervene.
Papal Territorial and Protectorate Settlement
Papal Protectorate Settlement

The Papal Provincial Settlement

Benevento, Pontecorvo, Perugia and Ancona have passed to Naples wherever they were held by the Pope. The remaining Papal State retains its theocratic government under southern protection. Its temporal administration will remain separate until a further Roman agreement follows victory over Piedmont. Land belonging to other states is outside these articles.
Protest the threat to the Papal States.
Reserve our position.
The Southern Demand upon Rome

Naples has challenged papal temporal authority outside Rome. Our government must decide whether to protest or reserve its position. This diplomatic response leaves our existing alliances, protection and freedom of action intact.
Take the French position into account.
Paris Protests the Papal Demand

French ministers have protested our challenge to papal temporal authority. Relations have deteriorated, and the court must weigh the danger of French intervention. The protest leaves French alliances and protection in force.
Continue the diplomatic exchanges.
Paris Reserves Its Position
French ministers have declined to protest the proposal immediately. Their restraint is an opening for diplomacy, not a promise of neutrality. Existing alliances and sphere protection remain in force.

Piedmont has accepted the articles offered under our current political programme. Ratification incorporates its territory into the southern state. A federal crown will preserve regional institutions, a constitutional crown will apply the common statute, and an absolute crown will govern through royal administration.
